description:
pkix-chain-simple/src/lib.rs:456-462 — the extension whitelist check:
  `if !allowed.contains(&ext.extn_id) {`
  `    if ext.critical { return Err(Error::UnhandledCriticalExtension { index }); }`
  `    else { return Err(Error::UnexpectedExtension { index }); }`
  `}`

This loop short-circuits on the FIRST non-allowed extension. If there are two non-allowed extensions on a cert (one critical, one non-critical), the error depends on which appears first in the DER extension sequence — not necessarily which is more severe.

If the non-critical non-allowed extension comes first, it returns UnexpectedExtension even if there's a critical non-allowed extension later. Callers who receive UnexpectedExtension may not realize there's also an UnhandledCriticalExtension lurking.

This is a minor diagnostic issue (not a security issue: both cases result in rejection). P3 — but notable because pkix-chain-simple is meant to give clear error messages.
title: pkix-chain-simple check_extensions: non-critical extension error reported as UnexpectedExtension, not per-type error
